Theo van Doesburg was a Dutch artist born in Utrecht in 1883. In 1917 he founded the magazine De Stijl with Piet Mondrian and others, promoting art made of straight lines and primary colors, and he also designed buildings and stained glass. He lived in the Netherlands, France and Germany and died in Davos, Switzerland, in 1931.

Albert Gleizes was a French painter born in Paris in 1881. He was one of the artists who invented Cubism and wrote an important book about it with Jean Metzinger. He lived in Paris and New York, and later in the south of France, where he died in 1953.

August Macke was a German painter born in Meschede in 1887. He lived in Bonn and Munich and was a member of the Blue Rider group, painting happy scenes of parks and shop windows in bright colors. He was killed in World War I in France in 1914 at the age of 27.

Hilma af Klint was a Swedish artist born near Stockholm in 1862. She trained as a painter and in 1906 began making huge abstract paintings, years before the famous pioneers of abstract art, but she asked that they not be shown until 20 years after her death. She died in 1944, and her work became world famous in the 2000s.

Joseph Stella was an Italian-born American painter, born in Muro Lucano, Italy, in 1877. He moved to New York at 19, painted its bridges, factories and amusement parks in a bold Futurist style and is best known for his images of the Brooklyn Bridge. He died in New York in 1946.

Marianne von Werefkin was a Russian painter born in Tula in 1860. She studied with Ilya Repin, moved to Munich, and helped found the Blue Rider group, though she is less known than her partner Alexej von Jawlensky. She lived the last years of her life in Ascona, Switzerland, and died there in 1938.

Luigi Russolo was an Italian Futurist painter and composer, born in Portogruaro in 1885. He painted pictures of speed and light and invented the 'intonarumori', noise-making machines that played the sounds of the modern city. He died in Laveno-Mombello in 1947.

Alexandra Exter was a Ukrainian-born Russian artist, born in Białystok in 1882. She knew the Cubists in Paris, taught in Kyiv and Moscow, and designed colorful scenery and costumes for theaters. She moved to France in 1924 and died near Paris in 1949.

Oscar Bluemner was a German-born American painter, born in Prenzlau in 1867. An architect by training, he moved to the United States in 1892 and made paintings of the New Jersey landscape in strong flat colors, especially red. He died in Braintree, Massachusetts, in 1938.

Kurt Schwitters was a German artist born in Hanover in 1887. He made collages and sculptures from scraps and trash that he called Merz, and also wrote poems and designed his own Merz Building. He left Germany when the Nazis came to power, lived in Norway and then in England, and died in Ambleside in 1948.

Ivan Kliun was a Russian painter born in 1873 near Moscow. He was an early follower of Kazimir Malevich and a leader of the Suprematists, who painted with pure geometric shapes. He lived in Moscow and died there in 1943.

Marsden Hartley was an American painter born in Lewiston, Maine, in 1877. He traveled to Paris and Berlin, where he made bold abstract paintings of flags, symbols and military insignia, and later returned to paint his native Maine. He died in Ellsworth, Maine, in 1943.

Alexej von Jawlensky was a Russian painter born in Torzhok in 1864. He served as an army officer, moved to Munich to paint and became part of the Blue Rider circle, famous for faces painted in bold colors. He died in Wiesbaden, Germany, in 1941.

Robert Delaunay was a French painter born in Paris in 1885. With his wife Sonia, he invented a colorful style called Orphism and painted the Eiffel Tower, windows and circles of color. He spent the war years in Spain and Portugal, and died in Montpellier in 1941.

Olga Rozanova was a Russian painter born in Melenki in 1886. She was a leading woman of the Russian avant-garde who worked with Malevich on Suprematism and designed books and textiles. She died of diphtheria in Moscow in 1918 at the age of 32.

Lyubov Popova was a Russian painter and designer born near Moscow in 1889. She studied in Paris, became a leader of the avant-garde in Moscow, and designed theater sets and fabrics for the new Soviet state. She died of scarlet fever in Moscow in 1924 at the age of 35.

Ilya Chashnik was a Russian artist born in Ludza, now in Latvia, in 1902. He was a student of Kazimir Malevich and worked in the Suprematist group in Vitebsk and Petrograd, painting geometric shapes and designing porcelain. He died in 1929 at the age of 26.

Juan Gris was a Spanish painter born in Madrid in 1887. He moved to Paris in 1906, became a friend of Picasso and one of the leading Cubists, painting clear and colorful still lifes. He died in Paris in 1927 at the age of 40.

Patrick Henry Bruce was an American painter born in Campbell County, Virginia, in 1881. He lived in Paris for most of his career, studied with Matisse and painted bright, rhythmic pictures of shapes and objects. He returned to New York, where he died in 1936.

Arthur Dove was an American painter born in Canandaigua, New York, in 1880. He is considered one of the first American artists to paint abstractly, painting nature, music and feelings, often while living on a boat or in a farmhouse on Long Island. He died in Huntington, New York, in 1946.
